submission.justification:
Conditional recommendation. Mixture-G2 at a 1.8 mm gap gave the best simulated time resolution (0.887 ns). That beats the 2 mm baseline (0.9 ns for G2, 1.3 ns for G3, 2 ns for G1). The scan for G2 covered 1 mm (value recorded), 1.8 mm (0.887 ns), 1.9 mm (0.907 ns) and 3 mm (1.082 ns), so 1.8 mm is the best of the points tested. The gap of 1.8 mm is within the 1–3 mm range.

The GWP100 hard requirement (<=150) is NOT verified. None of the six project documents records a GWP100 value or a gas composition for any candidate, so no candidate passed the check and none was excluded. G2 was selected on performance alone. It must not be adopted or deployed until its GWP100 is confirmed at or below 150 from the candidate specification or a supplier/lab source. If G2 fails that check, the fallback is G3 (1.3 ns baseline at 2 mm), since G1 is the slowest. The gap optimum for G3 or G1 was not simulated.

Also note: the simulation count fields in the results are inconsistent (0 and 4), and the 0.887 ns figure comes from a small number of runs, so the margin over the 2 mm baseline is modest (about 1.5%).

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible time resolution
requirements.evidence: Simulated G2 at 1.8 mm gives 0.887 ns, the best of the points tested (1 mm, 1.8, 1.9, 3 mm). This beats the 2 mm baseline of 0.9 ns for G2 and 1.3 ns for G3. Simulation-only result from a small number of runs; the optimum was not refined beyond the tested points and was not checked for G1 or G3 gaps.

requirements.evidence: This submission provides one mixture (Mixture-G2) and one gap (1.8 mm).
